record.context_brief: profit property of minimum replicating portfolios
record.original_question: For a contract with payoff P_T(S_1, ..., S_d) on d underlying assets, fix binomial upward and downward rates u_i and d_i for each asset. A portfolio V_0 = sum_i a_i S_i(0) + b is a binomial replicating portfolio if for every choice v_i in {d_i, u_i}, the terminal portfolio value sum_i a_i v_i S_i(0) + b is at least P_T(v_1 S_1(0), ..., v_d S_d(0)). A realistic-binomial replicating portfolio has the profit property when the writer's realized profit V_T - P_T is an increasing function of the deviations between the chosen rates and realized rates, namely u_i - u_i^* and d_i^* - d_i. Does the realistic binomial model produce a replicating portfolio with the profit property for any given option contract? If one chooses a minimum-initial-cost replicating portfolio among all replicating portfolios for a specific contract, does that minimum portfolio have the profit property, and if so what is the writer's probability of profit?

evidence.quote: We say that a replicating portfolio constructed by the (realistic) binomial model has the profit property for the contract X if the profit Π = VT − PT ... is increasing in every variable.

Problem 4. Does the (realistic) binomial model can produce a replicating portfolio with the profit property for any known contract?
The question is: does this portfolio has the profit property for a specific contract? If yes, what is the probability of profit for the writer?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-period market with $d$ risky assets having initial prices $S_1(0),\dots,S_d(0)>0$. For each asset $i$, fix two positive numbers $d_i<u_i$, interpreted as a downward and an upward gross return so that the terminal price of asset $i$ takes one of the two values $d_i S_i(0)$ or $u_i S_i(0)$. (For simplicity assume zero interest rate.) Let $P_T:\mathbb{R}_+^d	o\mathbb{R}$ be the payoff of a European contract on these $d$ assets.

A portfolio with initial value
$$V_0 \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^d a_i\, S_i(0) + b,$$
where $a_i\in\mathbb{R}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$ is a cash position, is called a binomial replicating (super-replicating) portfolio for $P_T$ if, for every choice $(v_1,\dots,v_d)\in\prod_{i=1}^d\{d_i,u_i\}$,
$$\sum_{i=1}^d a_i\, v_i\, S_i(0) + b \;\ge\; P_T igl(v_1 S_1(0),\dots,v_d S_d(0) igr).$$

Now assume the realized gross returns $v_i^{*}\in[d_i,u_i]$ may lie anywhere between the chosen bounds (the "realistic binomial" setting). The writer's realized profit is
$$\Pi \;=\; V_T - P_T(v_1^{*}S_1(0),\dots,v_d^{*}S_d(0)),\qquad V_T=\sum_i a_i v_i^{*}S_i(0)+b.$$
The replicating portfolio is said to have the profit property for the contract if $\Pi$ is a non-decreasing function of each of the deviations $u_i-v_i^{*}$ and $v_i^{*}-d_i$, $i=1,\dots,d$.

(a) Does the realistic binomial model always admit a replicating portfolio with the profit property, for every payoff $P_T$?

(b) Among all binomial replicating portfolios for a given payoff $P_T$, consider one of minimal initial cost $V_0$. Does such a minimum-cost replicating portfolio necessarily have the profit property? If it does, determine the writer's probability of profit, i.e.\ $\mathbb{P}(\Pi>0)$, under a specified (e.g.\ uniform on $\prod_i[d_i,u_i]$) distribution of the realized returns $(v_1^{*},\dots,v_d^{*})$.
